claims.text: A ConfigMap is an API object for configuration that is not confidential; it has data (and binaryData) fields holding key-value pairs instead of a spec, and is stored by the API server apart from Pods and images.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Configuration > ConfigMaps (overview; ConfigMap object)

claims.text: Values under a ConfigMap data field must be strings; an unquoted 1025 is read by YAML as a number and the API server rejects the ConfigMap, so the port is quoted.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: ConfigMaps (ConfigMap object: data designed to contain UTF-8 strings); ConfigMap API reference (data map[string]string)

claims.text: envFrom with a configMapRef in a container spec creates one environment variable per key of the named ConfigMap.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: ConfigMaps (Using ConfigMaps as environment variables: envFrom / configMapRef selects all key-value pairs)

claims.text: The kubelet sets a container env from the ConfigMap when it starts the container; env values are not updated in a running container, so a changed value reaches only containers started after the change.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: ConfigMaps ('ConfigMaps consumed as environment variables are not updated automatically and require a pod restart'); outputs configmap.txt

claims.text: Applying a changed ConfigMap does not change the Deployment's Pod template (or .metadata.generation), so no rollout starts; a rollout is triggered only by a .spec.template change.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Deployments (rollout triggered iff .spec.template changes); outputs/stage-2/scripts/k8s/configmap.txt ('changed: no')

claims.text: kubectl rollout restart deployment/<name> replaces all the Deployment's Pods through a rolling update without changing the image; the new containers get the ConfigMap's current values.
claims.source_hint: kubectl rollout restart reference; outputs configmap.txt (2525 after restart)

claims.text: ASP.NET Core maps '__' in an environment variable name to ':' in the configuration key, so Smtp__Port sets Smtp:Port (taught in devops.l1.config-and-env).
claims.source_hint: learn.microsoft.com: Configuration in ASP.NET Core (Environment variables, double underscore)

claims.text: api-configmap.yaml@stage-2: ConfigMap api, 5 data keys equal to docker-compose.yml api env; hosts are Service names except Keycloak__Authority (issuer written into tokens, localhost:8180); api reaches Keycloak via MetadataAddress.
claims.source_hint: git -C examples/don-hang show stage-2:deploy/k8s/api-configmap.yaml and stage-2:docker-compose.yml (api environment)

claims.text: deploy/k8s/api.yaml@stage-2: the api container has envFrom: - configMapRef: name: api (lines 30-32).
kubectl exec deployment/<name> -- <cmd> runs the command in a container of one Pod of that Deployment.
claims.source_hint: kubectl exec reference (TYPE/NAME form selects a Pod of the workload)

claims.text: A Deployment's .metadata.generation increases when its spec changes (not when another object such as a ConfigMap changes).
configmap.sh output@stage-2: printenv shows 1025 after applying Smtp__Port 2525 and 'changed: no'; after rollout restart printenv shows 2525; the script then re-applies the file and restarts again.
A ConfigMap provides no secrecy or encryption: anyone allowed to read ConfigMaps in the namespace can print its values in plain text (kubectl get configmap -o yaml).
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: ConfigMaps (caution: 'ConfigMap does not provide secrecy or encryption')
